title: Consolidate SDK streaming ergonomics & retries; standardize release pipeline and artifact signing
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Objective:
Unify streaming ergonomics, retry semantics, and example patterns across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, and implement a hardened release pipeline that publishes signed artifacts to PyPI/npm/go modules with verifiable provenance. This ticket covers design decisions, CI changes, and end-to-end publishing steps (including signing and SBOM provenance).

Background and motivation:
- Multiple SDKs implemented ad-hoc streaming and retry behavior leading to inconsistent developer experience (differences in reconnects, visible resumption tokens, and backpressure handling).
- Release process is fragile: manual tagging, inconsistent publishing commands, no consistent artifact signing/provenance for downstream customers needing compliance.
- Goal: a single set of ergonomics (idiomatic per-language) and a repeatable CI->publish flow with reproducible artifacts and signatures (GPG/Sigstore/cosign where applicable).

Design summary (high level):
1) Retry semantics:
   - Expose a RetryPolicy object with fields: max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter (true/false), retryable_codes.
   - Default: conservative retries for idempotent RPCs (embeddings, stateless generation calls with seedempotency) and disabled for non-idempotent streaming by default.
   - Allow opt-in automatic retries for streaming when callers provide an idempotency key and resume_token handling.

2) Streaming ergonomics:
   - Python: async iterator pattern that yields Message objects and exposes a .resume_token attribute when available; provide helper method .resume_from(token). Example usage: async for chunk in client.stream_generate(...):
       if chunk.resume_token: save_token(chunk.resume_token)
   - TypeScript: AsyncIterable<ResponseChunk> with a StreamController helper that handles optional auto-reconnect when resume token provided. Provide small high-level helper streamWithRetries(options) for typical use.
   - Go: channel-based iterator with context for cancellation and a ResumeToken struct for manual resumption.
   - Backpressure: SDKs will not buffer unbounded. Streams expose an optional prefetch_count and a configurable buffer_limit; default = 4 chunks.

3) Idempotency & resume protocol:
   - Server will accept an idempotency_key + resume_token pair to resume interrupted streams for up to 5 minutes.
   - SDKs emit resume_token with each checkpoint (every N tokens or on explicit checkpoint API).

4) Examples & Recipes:
   - Provide a cookbook folder in each repo with examples: graceful-shutdown, reconnecting-streams, resumable-transcripts, and unit tests demonstrating lesion scenarios.

Release engineering: CI and artifact signing plan:
- CI pipeline changes (GitHub Actions):
  1. On tag push vX.Y.Z: run build, run SDK language tests, generate SBOM (syft), run tox/unit/integration matrix.
  2. Produce distribution artifacts in a release workspace: Python wheels + sdist, npm packages (pack), Go modules + zip.
  3. Generate checksums (sha256) and sign them with Sigstore/cosign where supported; attach in-toto provenance statement including git revision, build env, SBOM URL.
  4. Sign git tag with GPG (developer step pre-release) and upload release assets to GitHub Releases.

- Publishing steps per language (automated via GH Actions):
  - Python: build wheel and sdist, run twine check, upload to private PyPI or TestPyPI during staging; production to PyPI requires Sigstore attestation + GPG-signed tag. Example commands used in CI: python -m build; twine check dist/*; python -m twine upload --repository pypi dist/* --sign (CI uses sigstore integration).
  - TypeScript/npm: npm pack, run npm audit/fix, ci uses npm publish --access public/private with 2FA token injected via GH secrets; attach cosign signature for tarball using cosign.
  - Go: module proxy-friendly release: push git tag, ensure go.sum consistency, build zip artifacts and publish to GitHub Releases; publish checksums + cosign signatures for module zips.

- Provenance and attestation:
  - Use Sigstore (rekor + cosign) in CI to sign each artifact produced. For languages that don't have native cosign integration for package registries, attach an in-toto SLSA attestation JSON describing inputs and sign that with cosign and upload to the release assets.
  - Generate SBOM using Syft and attach to release.
  - Add a verification script (tools/verify_release.sh) that: verifies GPG-signed tag, verifies cosign signatures, checks SBOM existence, and validates sha256 checksums.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full deterministic builds vs. pragmatic reproducibility: achieving bit-for-bit deterministic builds across GH Actions runners is costly; we opt for strong attestation (SBOM + cosign + pinned builder image) rather than full reproducibility in first pass.
- User ergonomics vs explicit control: streaming auto-reconnect by default can hide failures; we choose default=off with a one-line opt-in helper to enable auto-resume if callers provide idempotency.

Key artifacts and links (in-repo):
- GH Action workflow: .github/workflows/release-sdk.yml (PR #1423)

acceptance_criteria: SDKs for Python/TS/Go expose consistent retry policy objects and default semantics documented in the README.
Streaming APIs in each SDK support resume_token semantics with example recipes and unit/integration tests covering interruption and resume.
CI release workflow builds artifacts and produces SBOM + cosign-signed attestation for every tagged release.
A verification script exists that validates tag signatures, artifact cosign signatures, and SBOM presence.
Security review completed and sign-off obtained before first public release; all requested hardening actions tracked in sub-issues.
